subject: Re: Economics scan — hyperscaler assumption gaps & staged test plan
messages:
From: Jennifer Park <jennifer@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: John Thompson <john.t@acme.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo notes: token economics questions

Thanks for the demo this morning — good conversation. A couple of follow-ups from our finance/infra folks:

- Can you share a clear per-1M tokens cost estimate for the configuration you demoed (gpt-13b-quant with 8K context) vs the hyperscaler managed endpoint we currently use? Our procurement team needs a delta to justify a pilot.
- We use aggressive batching on the hyperscaler (avg batch size ~24). Do you expect similar gains in Redwood with continuous batching, or do the latency SLOs change the calculus?
- What cache hit rate should we assume for a conversational product that includes 20% repeated system/context tokens per session?

I attached the token distribution sample and their current invoice lines. Can we get a one-page summary and a short test plan that we can show to our infra lead?

Thanks,
Jennifer
Director of Product
Acme AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jennifer Park <jennifer@acme.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes: token economics questions

Jennifer — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the invoice lines. Attached is a short spreadsheet with modeled per-1M-token numbers and the proposed staged test plan (high level). Key takeaways up front:

1) Baseline per-1M tokens (hosted managed hyperscaler): ~USD 44–56 / 1M tokens depending on their batching and discount assumptions.
2) Redwood hosted profile (gpt-13b-quant, 8K): modeled range ~USD 21–32 / 1M tokens for production mix we discussed (median seq len 120). Primary savings drivers are continuous batching + prefix KV cache.
3) Batching sensitivity: at avg batch=24 the hyperscaler achieves ~35–45% per-token savings vs single-request execution; Redwood with continuous batching + optimized kernel scheduling shows similar or better unit economics but with predictable latency tails (p99 + fallback path).
4) Cache hit realistic assumption: for your stated 20% repeated context tokens, we model a 28–42% effective token-level cache hit (depends on session stickiness and prompt templating). That yields an incremental 10–18% reduction in per-1M cost.

I've included a proposed three-stage test plan in the attachment:
- Stage A (bench): 100k synthetic requests matching your token distribution to validate baseline per-token numbers and latency SLO.
- Stage B (pilot): 72-hour routed pilot for a subset of production traffic (10% of users) to measure real cache hit and batch distributions.
- Stage C (validation): 1M-token run with production client to finalize negotiated pricing and model pin.

Next steps I propose: 1) confirm pilot window and target endpoints, 2) grant us a sample of 48 hours of production logs (anonymized) to tune batching thresholds, 3) schedule a short technical sync with your infra lead to validate network/topology assumptions.

Ben/Karthik — can you review the attached numbers and confirm the benchmarking script we should run for Stage A?

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jennifer Park <jennifer@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes: token economics questions

Quick reality check and proposed bench config:

Marissa — spreadsheet looks reasonable. A few clarifications before we lock Stage A:
- For the "Redwood modeled range" please ensure we show both 50th and 95th percentile per-token CPU/GPU utilization over the sample because Acme cares about burst vs steady-state pricing.
- Bench script: 120-token median prompts, 8% heavy prompts (~1.8k tokens), Poisson inter-arrival to mimic user bursts. Continuous batching window = 12ms target, but we should parameterize 6/12/24ms to capture sensitivity.
- Cache assumptions: we should test three hit-rate scenarios (20%, 35%, 55%) and report incremental per-1M delta for each. We'll capture token-level breakdown and compute both raw model cost and system-overhead (network, routing) contribution.

I attached a short runbook for running the bench (runbook_batching_cache_tests.pdf). Karthik — can you assign the bench job on the dedicated cluster and add the autodump for KV cache stats?

Ben
Director of Solutions | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jennifer Park <jennifer@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes: token economics questions

Ben / Marissa — acknowledged. I'll schedule the bench on the dedicated cluster for tomorrow morning and parameterize the batching windows and cache-hit profiles Ben requested. Deliverables we'll produce after Stage A (48–72 hr bench):

- Per-1M token cost table (50th/95th) for each batch window and cache-hit row.
- Latency tail analysis (p50/p95/p99) and a fallback-model routing impact assessment.
- A short doc listing assumptions that differ from the hyperscaler (pricing cadence, preemption risk, and network egress assumptions) so Acme's finance team can reconcile line items.

Jennifer — can you confirm 1) an internal contact for the anonymized logs, and 2) whether the pilot needs SOC2/compliance prechecks (if yes, we'll place the pilot behind a dedicated VPC for auditability).

We'll follow up with the bench results and a recommended pricing band.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Platform Solutions | Redwood Inference
